title: Science One Framework: A verifiable autonomous research framework via Chain-of-Evidence
excerpt: Google Research introduced Science One, an autonomous research framework that natively builds verifiable evidence chains behind every claim an AI system makes. In their evaluation the approach cut phantom-reference rates in AI-generated scientific papers from 21% to zero.
rationale: Turns the biggest blocker to AI-written science, fabricated citations, into an engineered guarantee measured from 21% to zero.

title: Four labs find experimental differences can undermine AI catalyst predictions
excerpt: A four-laboratory round-robin led by SLAC found that tiny procedural differences, above all mixing intensity, produced inconsistent catalyst measurements, meaning the datasets used to train materials ML models can encode lab artifacts rather than chemistry. The authors argue standardized protocols and metadata are a precondition for AI-driven catalysis.
rationale: A rare multi-lab reproducibility check showing AI-for-materials can learn lab habits instead of chemistry, changing how these datasets must be built.

title: Solving the solvent problem
excerpt: An AI-guided algorithm generated 100,000 candidate solvent molecules, which MIT researchers narrowed to 200 and then synthesized, finding that shrinking solvent size breaks the usual trade-off between ion transport speed and electrolyte stability in sodium-metal batteries.
rationale: A complete AI-to-bench loop: 100,000 generated candidates down to synthesized molecules that break a long-standing electrolyte trade-off.

title: The benefits of medical AI assistance vary based on user expertise
excerpt: In an MIT study of skin-disease diagnosis, AI assistance raised accuracy for both clinicians and non-experts, but non-experts deferred to the model even when it was wrong, while clinicians more often caught its mistakes. Expertise, not the model, determined who benefited.
rationale: Quantifies who actually gains from AI assistance and who merely inherits its errors, the core question for any human-in-the-loop deployment.

title: The OlmoEarth Platform: Geospatial inference at planetary scale
excerpt: Ai2 detailed the infrastructure behind OlmoEarth, letting researchers fine-tune geospatial foundation models and run continent-scale satellite inference in about a day at fractions of a penny per square kilometer, turning Earth-observation science into a routine query.
rationale: Open infrastructure that drops continent-scale Earth observation to a day and pennies per square kilometer, putting planetary remote sensing within reach of ordinary labs.
